shared_topics.title: Iran War: US Strikes Paused, 600+ Casualties, Diplomatic Limbo
shared_topics.correlation_label: Same event, materially different framing — left emphasizes human cost and political opposition; right emphasizes strategic rationale and public support for completing the mission.
shared_topics.summary: The US paused new lethal strikes against Iran on July 27 after 13 consecutive nights of bombing, with UN envoy Mike Waltz saying Trump is giving diplomacy 'some space.' Iran's foreign ministry denied any current negotiations are underway. Pentagon confirmed casualties have surpassed 600 and quietly revised its accounting methodology. Oman is leading regional diplomatic efforts. A CBS News/YouGov poll found 57% of Americans frustrated with the war, while a separate Breitbart-commissioned poll claims a majority supports seeing the conflict through.

left.framing: Left outlets frame the pause as a potential off-ramp from a costly, unauthorized war. CNN reported the Pentagon 'quietly changed' its casualty accounting as deaths crossed 600, raising military transparency alarms. The Daily Beast highlighted that 57% of Americans are frustrated with the war Trump launched without congressional authorization. NBC detailed the third consecutive night of strikes before the pause and the deaths of multiple US service members.

right.framing: Right outlets frame the pause as a tactical decision on the way to strategic victory, not a retreat. Fox News focused on the battle for control of the Strait of Hormuz as the central strategic prize. Breitbart ran an exclusive poll claiming a majority of Americans believe the US must 'finish the job.' National Review's weekly wrap treated the Iran war's resumption as a necessary response to Iranian aggression, with minimal criticism of the cost.

shared_topics.title: 100 Days to Midterms: Both Parties Claim Advantage
shared_topics.correlation_label: Both sides agree on the competitive landscape; they diverge sharply on which structural advantages matter most heading into November.
shared_topics.summary: With exactly 100 days until the November 3 midterm elections, both parties are making competing claims about their position. Democrats point to an 11-point generic ballot advantage, a 10-point enthusiasm edge, and a favorable House environment. Republicans counter with a 5-to-1 cash advantage ($677M vs. $136M), redistricting gains, and an NRCC memo targeting 36 Democratic House seats. Independent forecasters favor Democrats for the House but see Republicans as slight favorites to retain the Senate.

left.framing: Left outlets frame the 100-day mark as a Democratic wave building: voters are energized, the generic ballot is historically favorable, and Republicans are weighed down by Trump's declining approval and the Iran war. The Hill's new poll shows Democrats up 11 points with a 10-point enthusiasm edge — 8 points higher than the 2018 blue wave. Axios reported Democrats are outperforming Kamala Harris in virtually every special election.

right.framing: Right outlets emphasize Republican structural advantages that could offset the generic ballot: the NRCC holds a $13.7M cash-on-hand edge over the DCCC, MAGA Inc. has a $400M war chest, and the GOP's total cash advantage is 5-to-1. Fox News highlighted redistricting gains and a 36-seat targeting map. Breitbart focused on the $677M vs $136M disparity as evidence of Republican organizational strength.

shared_topics.title: SAVE Act Standoff: Trump vs. Thune on Voter ID Before Recess
shared_topics.correlation_label: Both sides report the same legislative standoff; they diverge on whether the SAVE Act is voter protection or voter suppression, and whether Thune is right to resist.
shared_topics.summary: President Trump demanded Senate Majority Leader John Thune cancel the August recess unless the SAVE America Act — which would require photo ID for federal elections — passes before the break. Thune pushed back, saying there are insufficient votes for the bill, which has previously failed despite pressure from the White House. The White House publicly stated Trump's patience with Thune is 'running out.' The standoff reflects ongoing tension between the House-passed reconciliation agenda and Senate reluctance.

left.framing: Left outlets frame Trump's pressure as an attempt to ram through voter restriction legislation using executive bullying. The New Republic described Thune 'snapping' at Trump over the demand, casting it as resistance to election manipulation. Axios covered it as a legislative power struggle with Thune holding firm against undue presidential pressure.

right.framing: Right outlets frame the SAVE Act as a popular, common-sense voter integrity measure that Congress is failing to pass. The Washington Examiner detailed the White House's lobbying of 20 GOP senators to nuke procedural hurdles, framing Thune's resistance as a failure of legislative courage. Breitbart ran a poll showing majority voter support for the bill.

gap_left.title: Democrats Build Anti-Iran War Legislative Coalition for Midterms
gap_left.summary: Left-leaning outlets are covering the Democratic Party's strategic decision to make the Iran war their defining midterm issue. CNN reported that the war has become the most partisan military engagement in modern US history, with Democrats in lockstep opposing it from the start. The New Republic detailed the legislative effort by Reps. Smith, Aguilar, and Lieu to pass a war powers resolution — which cleared the House 214-208 before being blocked in the Senate by Republicans. The Hill covered Democratic leaders preparing a second war powers push. Right media covers the war itself but does not frame Democratic opposition as a coherent electoral strategy.

gap_left.title: CNN Analysis: Trump's Economic Approval Collapse Is the GOP's Core 2026 Problem
gap_left.summary: CNN published a July 28 analysis showing Trump's approval has declined steadily on two key metrics: 85% of independents and a majority of Republicans (58%) say his administration hasn't focused enough on economic issues — both record highs for his second term. The piece frames this not as a general approval story but as the specific electoral liability Republicans face entering the final 100 days. Right media covers Republican cash advantages and redistricting but does not frame Trump's declining economic approval as a structural GOP problem.

gap_left.title: DCCC Expands Red to Blue Slate — Five New House Target Seats Added
gap_left.summary: The Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee announced it is adding five new candidates to its 'Red to Blue' program, which identifies competitive House seats it aims to flip from Republican. The expansion signals Democratic confidence in an expanded offensive map with 100 days to go. The Hill covered the announcement as part of a broader Democratic offensive targeting Republican-held districts. Right media focuses on the NRCC's competing cash advantage and redistricting map but does not cover the DCCC's recruitment program as a standalone story.

gap_left.title: Iran War Analysis: At Every Decision Point, Trump's Options Are Getting Worse
gap_left.summary: CNN's analytical coverage of the Iran war goes beyond day-to-day reporting to examine Trump's strategic decision-making. The July 27 analysis found that at each fork in the road — escalate, negotiate, or withdraw — Trump's available choices have deteriorated. Slate's Political Gabfest covered similar terrain, noting Trump is simultaneously unable to 'win' and politically unwilling to stand down. The American Conservative noted a bipartisan anti-war movement is emerging, but left outlets are specifically framing Trump's personal decision-making as the driving problem, an angle absent from right-leaning coverage.

gap_right.title: NJ DMV Error Puts 6,600 Noncitizens on Voter Rolls; DOJ Demands Records
gap_right.summary: A software error in New Jersey's DMV system registered approximately 6,600 noncitizens to vote, with approximately 400 casting ballots in at least one election. The DOJ formally demanded New Jersey produce voter roll records within five days. The Federalist ran the story as direct evidence of the need for the SAVE Act; Daily Wire covered it as part of broader Democratic voter registration failures. Left outlets have largely framed the NJ situation as an isolated software malfunction; right outlets treat it as a systemic election integrity problem requiring federal action.

gap_right.title: Hawaii Democratic Lt. Governor Indicted on Bribery Charges
gap_right.summary: An Oahu grand jury indicted Hawaii Lt. Governor Sylvia Luke, a Democrat, on bribery charges related to an alleged scheme involving campaign contributions in exchange for securing state funding for COVID-19 testing contracts while she served as a state lawmaker in 2022. Townhall and right-leaning outlets covered the indictment prominently as evidence of Democratic corruption. Left-leaning national outlets have not given this story significant coverage.

gap_right.title: Jay Clayton Confirmed as DNI — Section 702 FISA Tool Back Online
gap_right.summary: The Senate advanced Jay Clayton's nomination as Director of National Intelligence, with a final confirmation vote clearing a key procedural hurdle. Fox News and the Washington Examiner covered the confirmation as a Trump administration win that will restart the Section 702 FISA counterterrorism surveillance tool, which had lapsed during the vacancy. Left outlets have not covered Clayton's confirmation as a major news event despite the national security implications.

gap_right.title: Conservative and Bipartisan Anti-Iran War Movement Gaining Ground
gap_right.summary: The American Conservative is covering the emergence of a bipartisan anti-war coalition that includes right-leaning voices — a story left outlets are not telling. TAC featured a conversation with Ana Kasparian on the shared ground between libertarian conservatives and the left on Iran war opposition. TAC also reported that Vance and Joint Chiefs chair Caine both raised Iran escalation concerns in a White House meeting. This conservative anti-war frame — distinct from progressive opposition — receives no coverage in left-leaning media, which focuses on Democratic Party opposition.
